title: startkde on systemd: safeguard against already started plasma session in another user session
line: Logging in to Plasma a second time as the same user now returns with a clear message instead of a black screen, and the running session is no longer logged out.
explanation: systemd runs one graphical-session.target per user, so a second Plasma login for the same user (another VT or seat) could never start: startplasma-wayland synced its environment over the running session's, asked systemd to start targets that were already active and then sat on a black screen. When that second login ended, its cleanup stopped plasma-workspace.target, which logged out the first session too. startplasma-wayland now asks systemd whether graphical-session.target is already active (or activating) before touching anything, and if so prints a message (also through xmessage when possible) and exits, so the login manager returns to the greeter.

commits.message:
startkde: refuse to start when a graphical session is already running

systemd allows only one graphical-session.target per user, so a second
login for the same user showed a black screen and, when it gave up, also
stopped the running session. Now check first and exit with a message.

BUG: 464045

media.caption: Master: the second login does nothing, and when it ends the first session's graphical-session, plasmashell and KWin are all stopped
With the fix: the second login exits at once with a message and the first session keeps running
